Repeat purchase rates by cohort and month (purchase = unique customer-day, repeat = at least one purchase in the target month):

Cohort sizes: January new users = 626, February new users = 715

|            | January new users | February new users |
|------------|-------------------|--------------------|
| February 2024 | 47.28% (296/626) |              |
| March 2024    | 38.02% (238/626) | 26.57% (190/715) |
| April 2024    | 39.30% (246/626) | 25.59% (183/715) |

Method: Deduplicated (Customer ID, Sales date) to count a single purchase per customer per day. A customer is in the January-new cohort if their first purchase month = 202401 (n=626) and in the February-new cohort if first purchase month = 202402 (n=715). Repeat purchase rate for month M = (customers in cohort with ≥1 purchase in M) / (cohort size).

question:
As the manager of a large supermarket chain, you have obtained detailed sales data for the period January through April 2024. If the same customer makes multiple purchases on the same day, it counts as a single purchase. Please analyze the following questions: Define users who made their first purchase in January 2024 as "January new users". Define users who made their first purchase in February 2024 and had never purchased before as "February new users".
1) For the "January new users" cohort, calculate their repeat purchase rate for each of February, March, and April. Repeat purchase is defined as: having at least one purchase in that month (regardless of product category).
2) For the "February new users" cohort, calculate their repeat purchase rate for each of March and April. Output in the table format below, |            | January new users | February new users |
|------------|------------|------------|
| February 2024 |      |            |
